items.text: **AC-9's stated assumption, made explicit and falsifiable**: because `checkFitScore()` for a listing is only ever called after that listing's own `scoreListing()` succeeds (AC-5), and `usage_cap`'s seeded ceilings are identical for `ai_scoring` and `ai_check` at every cadence (spec 0012 AC-8), the check tier's budget cannot be exhausted while the scoring tier's own budget still has room, PROVIDED every `ai_check` call in production is one this feature dispatches. Four named ways this can break, any one of which is reason to revisit AC-9: (1) this feature's sample rate is ever lowered below 1.0; (2) `usage_cap`'s two tiers are ever set to different ceilings; (3) a batch straddles a `usage_cap` window boundary (the daily and monthly caps reset on a UTC clock), since a listing scored just before the boundary can be checked just after it, spending against the new window's `ai_check` cap while the matching `ai_scoring` spend landed in the window that just closed, breaking the same window assumption even though the per listing ordering (score, then check) never does; (4) any future caller dispatches an `ai_check` call outside this feature's own scored-then-checked chain (a live test, a future eval of the check itself), which would consume budget this invariant does not account for.

If feature 16's eval harness later shows the five bands clustering rather than spreading (the condition **AC-2** defers to that harness), the band anchors in `rubric.ts` are the first thing to revise, not the vendor or any of this prompt's other instructions. **Still open, and its trigger has not fired.** Feature 16's harness ran the full sixteen pairs twice on 2026-09-08 and both runs observed all five bands, `strong_match` 35, `good_match` 5, `possible_match` 21, `weak_match` 11, `not_a_match` 8 in the first and 35, 4, 21, 8, 12 in the second, so the bands spread rather than clustered and AC-2's bar of at least three of five was already met. Spec 0018 did review the anchors, but for a different reason, two pairs disagreeing with their recorded expectation, and it concluded that `BAND_ANCHORS` holds and one committed expectation was wrong. No anchor changed and the hash is still `1b45f524b356`. So this item is neither satisfied nor superseded by that review; it is waiting on a clustering condition that has not been seen.

As a job seeker, I want a search to show me which jobs I already applied to,

A multi user job search web app: enter a profile, search real listings, see them ranked with the reasoning shown, click through to apply, and record that you applied. Free, no billing, built for the author's own job search plus a few friends and recruiters evaluating it as a portfolio piece.

_You are in charge. Every box below is a **suggestion**, not a gate: run any, skip any, and mark a feature `done` when you decide it is. The workflow records what you actually did (including "skipped"), it never requires a step. The one thing it asks is that a load bearing decision be written down (a spec), not that any check be run._

**AC-14**: The identity save Server Action, as this feature's representative write path, is driven once from a test with no browser (spec 0001's third runner constraint, deferred here by spec 0004's Follow up): fetch the page with the edit form open, read the rendered form's hidden action fields, and post them back; a redirect carrying the session cookie means it ran.
